title: Phileas Redaction Policy
description: Schema for a Phileas redaction policy JSON file. A policy defines which types of sensitive information to detect and how to redact or transform each type.

metadata.description: Optional descriptive information about the policy. Ignored during redaction.

config.description: Global configuration settings for the policy.

crypto.description: AES encryption settings used by the CRYPTO_REPLACE strategy.

fpe.description: Format-preserving encryption settings used by the FPE_ENCRYPT_REPLACE strategy.

identifiers.description: Defines which types of sensitive information to detect and how to handle each type.

ignored.description: Lists of terms to ignore globally during filtering.

ignoredPatterns.description: Regex patterns to ignore globally during filtering.

graphical.description: Graphical redaction settings for image and PDF redaction.

tabular.description: Column rules for tabular documents (CSV and Excel .xlsx): redact a whole column, leave it unchanged, or scan it with only some filters.

generators.description: Named, reusable replacement generators referenced by the MAP_REPLACE strategy's generator property.

metadata.description: Descriptive information about the policy, carried with the policy itself so it survives export, import, and sharing. Nothing here affects detection or redaction; an engine reads and writes it unchanged. Additional properties are allowed so the object can grow (author, timestamps, labels) without a breaking schema change.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the policy does.

validatorName.description: Name of a built-in checksum or structural validator the identifier filter may apply to its matches. The set is the source-of-truth catalog spec/v1.0/catalog/validators.yaml; this enum is kept in sync with it. Most national and financial identifiers reduce to the shared algorithms (luhn, mod11, mod97, mod23-letter); the remainder are specific named validators.

config.description: Global configuration settings for the policy.

splitting.description: Controls whether and how input text is split into smaller chunks before filtering.

review.description: Settings for selecting filter requests for human review.

email.description: Settings for redacting email messages beyond their text: headers removed outright, attachments, and inline images.

word.description: Settings for Word (.docx) and Rich Text (.rtf) documents beyond their body text: headers and footers, comments, tracked changes, hidden text, charts, embedded objects, and document properties.

excel.description: Settings for Excel (.xlsx) workbooks beyond their cell text: print headers and footers, charts, formula and pivot caches, embedded objects, and document properties.

csv.description: Settings for reading CSV documents: delimiter, quote character, and encoding.

splitting.description: Controls whether and how input text is split into smaller chunks before filtering.

threshold.description: Character count threshold above which text is split.

overlap.description: Number of characters each chunk shares with the end of the previous chunk when text is split. An entity that straddles a chunk boundary is still seen whole within the overlap window; spans detected in the overlap are de-duplicated and mapped back to their absolute document offsets. Default 0 (no overlap; chunks are contiguous).

redactionColor.description: Policy-wide color of the redaction box drawn over redacted text in PDFs, used for any span whose strategy does not set its own color. Accepts a named color (black, white, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, gray) or a 6-digit hex string matching ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$; an unrecognized or malformed value renders as black.

showReplacement.description: Whether to render replacement text inside the redaction box.

replacementFont.description: Font used for replacement text in PDFs.

replacementMaxFontSize.description: Maximum font size for replacement text in PDFs.

replacementFontColor.description: Color of the replacement text in PDFs.

compressionQuality.description: JPEG compression quality for PDF output (0.0 to 1.0).

preserveUnredactedPages.description: Whether to preserve pages that contain no redactions in their original form.

removeTrailingPeriods.description: Remove trailing periods from redacted output.

removeTrailingSpaces.description: Remove trailing spaces from redacted output.

removeTrailingNewLines.description: Remove trailing newlines from redacted output.

spanDisambiguation.description: Enable span disambiguation: the context-vector step that resolves which type an ambiguously-typed span is (for example SSN vs. phone number). Default true (current behavior). When false, this policy skips the disambiguation step. Subject to the global feature also being enabled: a policy can turn disambiguation off but not force it on when it is disabled globally.

review.description: Settings for selecting filter requests for human review: a random sample of requests, and a leftover check of the redacted output.

samplingRate.description: Probability, from 0.0 to 1.0, that a filter request is selected for human spot review, independent of what was detected. Selection is per request and stateless: a request is selected when a value drawn uniformly from [0, 1) is below the rate, drawn once per request even when the input is split into chunks. No count is kept per policy or shared between nodes, so the achieved rate converges on the configured one but is not exact for small volumes. Selection never changes the redacted output; the runtime reports it with the filter result (reviewSampled). Default 0.0 (no sampling).

leftoverCheck.description: A second detection pass over the redacted output that reports anything still detectable. The check never changes the redacted output. Findings exclude the values the redaction itself inserted (stand-ins from strategies such as RANDOM_REPLACE look like PII on purpose) and values on the policy's top-level ignore lists (ignored, ignoredPatterns). The policy's filters run in the check with their per-filter ignore lists (ignored, ignoredPatterns, ignoredFiles) stripped, and strategy conditions do not suppress a finding. Findings are what a scan of the reassembled output would give, even when the input is split into chunks. The runtime reports the check with the filter result: whether it was performed (and, when not, why, such as an output with no readable text, which is not reported as zero findings), the number of findings, and each finding's type, position in the output, and confidence. Findings do not carry the matched text in the result.

mode.description: When the check runs. off: never. onRequest: only when the caller asks for it through the runtime's API for that call. always: on every request; a caller cannot turn it off for a single call.

using.description: What the check detects with. broad: every filter the policy defines (including custom identifiers, dictionaries, and PhEye filters) as configured, plus every other built-in identifier at its defaults except the firstName and surname dictionaries, which match common words and run only as the policy defines them, so it finds kinds of information the policy did not cover; always a superset of samePolicy. samePolicy: only the policy's own filters, which confirms the policy took effect.

email.description: Settings for redacting email messages (.eml, and Outlook .msg written out as .eml) beyond their text. Subject, From, To, Cc, and every text body part (plain text, and HTML as markup) are always redacted by the policy's identifiers. Header names match case-insensitively. Removing a header removes the field entirely; removed headers are not scanned, and kept headers outside the redacted set are kept as they are. A message nested inside another (message/rfc822) is processed the same way, recursively. A signed message is redacted and its signature part dropped; an encrypted message is refused. The runtime reports, with the filter result, every attachment or inline image kept without being inspected, every attachment it removed because it could not redact it, and every dropped signature. In runtimes without email support this block has no effect.

removeTechnical.description: Removes the technical headers: Received, Return-Path, Message-ID, User-Agent, X-Mailer, X-MimeOLE, DKIM-Signature, Authentication-Results, Received-SPF, Autocrypt, and every header beginning X- or ARC-.

removeIdentity.description: Removes the identity headers: Bcc, Reply-To, Sender, and every header beginning Resent-.

removeDate.description: Removes the Date header, whatever its format, without relying on a date identifier.

removeSubject.description: Removes the Subject header instead of redacting it, for releases where even a redacted subject should not ship.

attachments.description: What happens to attachments. keep leaves them as they are, uninspected, and reports them. remove deletes them, including their filenames. redact redacts each attachment the runtime supports as a document (for example PDF, Word, Excel) with the same policy, and removes and reports any attachment it cannot redact.

inlineImages.description: What happens to images embedded in the body and referenced by cid:. keep leaves them, uninspected, and reports them. remove deletes them and neutralizes the references. Independent of attachments.

word.description: Settings for the parts of a Word (.docx) or Rich Text (.rtf) document outside its body text. Body text, footnotes, and endnotes are always redacted by the policy's identifiers. Author names and the authorship properties (dc:creator, cp:lastModifiedBy, Company, Manager, comment and revision authors, word/people.xml) are always cleared, and no setting keeps them. For .rtf, each setting applies where the format has the corresponding part; charts and highlight have no RTF counterpart and are ignored for it. In runtimes without Word or RTF support this block has no effect.

headersFooters.description: redact redacts the text of running headers and footers. keep leaves them unscanned. Images and page numbers in them are left as they are.

comments.description: remove deletes every comment, with its author. redact keeps comments and redacts their text.

trackedChanges.description: accept accepts every insertion and deletion and removes the revision history, so deleted text is gone. redact keeps the revisions and redacts their text, including deleted text.

hiddenText.description: remove deletes text marked hidden. redact keeps it and redacts it like visible text.

charts.description: redact redacts chart titles, labels, and cached data values. keep leaves them as they are.

uninspectableObjects.description: What happens to embedded objects the runtime cannot read (legacy OLE objects, other programs' files). remove deletes them. keep leaves them and reports them as uninspected. Embedded Word and Excel documents are always redacted in place.

removeDocumentProperties.description: Clears the document properties beyond the always-cleared authorship fields: title, subject, keywords, categories, the comments field, and custom properties. false clears only the authorship fields; it never keeps authorship.

highlight.description: Wraps each replacement in a highlight so a reviewer can find it.

excel.description: Settings for the parts of an Excel (.xlsx) workbook outside its cell text. Cell text and comments (legacy notes and threaded comments) are always redacted by the policy's identifiers. Author names and the authorship properties (dc:creator, cp:lastModifiedBy, Company, Manager, comment authors, persons) are always cleared, and no setting keeps them. In runtimes without Excel support this block has no effect.

printHeadersFooters.description: redact redacts print headers and footers. keep leaves them unscanned.

charts.description: redact redacts chart titles, labels, and cached data values. keep leaves them as they are.

formulaCaches.description: redact turns a formula whose cached result holds a detected value into a static redacted value, clears the remaining cached results, and sets the workbook to recalculate on open. keep leaves cached results as they are, so a cached copy of a redacted value may remain.

pivotCaches.description: redact redacts the pivot cache's copy of the source data and sets it to refresh on open. keep leaves it as it is.

uninspectableObjects.description: What happens to embedded objects the runtime cannot read (legacy OLE objects, other programs' files). remove deletes them. keep leaves them and reports them as uninspected. Embedded Word and Excel documents are always redacted in place.

removeDocumentProperties.description: Clears the document properties beyond the always-cleared authorship fields: title, subject, keywords, categories, the comments field, and custom properties. false clears only the authorship fields; it never keeps authorship.

csv.description: Settings for reading CSV documents. No effect on .xlsx. Column rules for CSV are in the top-level tabular section. In runtimes without CSV support this block has no effect.

delimiter.description: The field delimiter: one character, not a line break. Must differ from quote.

quote.description: The quote character around fields that contain the delimiter, a quote, or a line break: one character, not a line break. Must differ from delimiter.

encoding.description: The character encoding the document is read in, by its IANA name (for example UTF-8, ISO-8859-1).

crypto.description: AES-GCM encryption settings used by the CRYPTO_REPLACE strategy. A fresh random nonce is generated per value, so no initialization vector is configured. Values may be prefixed with 'env:' to read from environment variables.

key.description: AES encryption key. Prefix with 'env:' to read from an environment variable (e.g. 'env:CRYPTO_KEY').

fpe.description: Format-preserving encryption settings used by the FPE_ENCRYPT_REPLACE strategy. Values may be prefixed with 'env:' to read from environment variables.

key.description: FPE encryption key. Prefix with 'env:' to read from an environment variable.

tweak.description: FPE tweak value. Prefix with 'env:' to read from an environment variable.

ignored.description: A named list of terms to ignore during filtering.

files.description: Paths to files containing terms to ignore (one term per line).

ignoredPattern.description: A named regex pattern whose matches are ignored during filtering.

pattern.description: Java-compatible regular expression. Matches are excluded from filtering.

graphical.description: Graphical redaction settings for image and PDF redaction.

boundingBoxes.description: Fixed bounding boxes to redact in images or PDFs.

boundingBox.description: A rectangular region to redact in an image or PDF page.

color.description: Fill color for the redaction box. Accepts a named color (black, white, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, gray) or a 6-digit hex string matching ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$; an unrecognized or malformed value renders as black.

x.description: X coordinate of the top-left corner.

y.description: Y coordinate of the top-left corner.

tabular.description: Column rules for tabular documents: CSV and Excel (.xlsx). Each column is handled by its own rule, all in one pass over the cells: a column with a rule follows it, and a column without one follows its sheet's unlistedColumns, by default scanned with every filter in identifiers. Header rows are never redacted. With an empty identifiers and the default unlistedColumns, only columns with a rule are changed. A runtime that does not support tabular rules must reject a policy that sets this section rather than ignore it, since ignoring it would leave columns unredacted without warning. Per-request options that pick columns (for example an interactive column picker) override the policy's rules for that request.

sheets.description: Sheet entries: at most one per worksheet name, and at most one without a worksheet. An .xlsx worksheet follows the entry that names it, or else the entry without a worksheet, if there is one. A CSV is one unnamed sheet, so only the entry without a worksheet applies to it.

tabularSheet.description: Column rules for one worksheet, or for every worksheet without an entry of its own and for a CSV document.

worksheet.description: Worksheet name, matched case-insensitively, as Excel compares sheet names. When absent, the entry applies to every worksheet without an entry of its own and to a CSV document. No effect on CSV: an entry that names a worksheet never applies to a CSV.

headerRows.description: Number of leading header rows. Header rows are never redacted. A column rule's header is matched against the last header row. 0 means the sheet has no header row, and columns can only be picked by index.

unlistedColumns.description: What happens to columns without a rule. identifiers scans them with every filter in identifiers. ignore leaves them unchanged. redact replaces every data cell whole with unlistedStrategies, with no detection, so only columns with a rule (for example ignore) survive unchanged.

unlistedStrategies.description: The strategies that replace the data cells of columns without a rule when unlistedColumns is redact. Allowed only then. Defaults to a single REDACT strategy.

columns.description: Column rules. At most one rule per header and per index.

tabularColumn.description: A rule for one column, picked by exactly one of header or index.

header.description: Matched against the displayed text of the column's cell in the last header row, trimmed: a formula by its result, rich text as plain text, and a merged cell by its top-left value. When several columns share the header, the rule applies to every one of them. A header that matches no column is reported as a warning, not an error, since one policy may cover files whose columns differ.

action.description: redact replaces every data cell whole with strategies, with no detection, whatever identifiers contains; malformed and partial values are replaced too. ignore leaves the data cells unchanged. filter scans each data cell with only the filters named in filters and replaces only what they find, so detection is probabilistic, as it is for identifiers.

strategies.description: The strategies a redact rule replaces each data cell with. Required for redact and not allowed otherwise. The %t placeholder in redactionFormat expands to full-column.

filters.description: The filters a filter rule scans each data cell with, by their key in identifiers (for example pheyes, emailAddress). Each must be defined in identifiers, and a key that holds several filters, such as pheyes (every DETECT PHEYE filter), uses all of them. Required for filter and not allowed otherwise.

columnStrategy.description: A strategy that replaces a whole cell: a filter strategy without a condition, since a whole-column rule replaces every cell. Consistent pseudonymization (replacementScope), CRYPTO_REPLACE, and FPE_ENCRYPT_REPLACE work as they do for a filter.

identifiers.description: Defines which types of sensitive information to detect and how to handle each type.

canadaSin.description: Detects Canadian Social Insurance Numbers (nine digits, Luhn-validated, format NNN-NNN-NNN).

city.description: Detects city names using dictionary matching.

county.description: Detects county names using dictionary matching.

date.description: Detects date values in various formats.

deaNumber.description: Detects DEA registration numbers (two letters, or a letter and 9, followed by seven digits, validated by the check digit, format AB1234563).

deviceIdentifier.description: Detects medical device identifiers and serial numbers (HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier (M)): GS1 and HIBCC UDIs by their check digit or character, with no cue word, and serial numbers that follow a cue word such as 'S/N' within windowSize tokens. patterns replaces the default serial number pattern; the UDI checks always apply.

dictionaries.description: Custom dictionary filters. Each entry defines a set of terms to detect.

ein.description: Detects U.S. Employer Identification Numbers (federal tax ID, format NN-NNNNNNN).

firstName.description: Detects first names using dictionary matching.

healthPlanMemberId.description: Detects health plan beneficiary and member IDs (HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier (I)) that follow a cue word such as 'Member ID' within windowSize tokens.

hospital.description: Detects hospital names using dictionary matching.

identifiers.description: Custom regex-based identifier filters. Each entry defines a pattern to detect.

itin.description: Detects U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (SSN-shaped, beginning with 9, format 9XX-XX-XXXX).

mbi.description: Detects Medicare Beneficiary Identifiers (eleven characters in the format CMS publishes, such as 1EG4-TE5-MK73).

medicalCondition.description: Detects medical conditions using PhEye AI-based detection.

medicalRecordNumber.description: Detects medical record numbers (HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier (H)) that follow a cue word such as 'MRN' within windowSize tokens.

npi.description: Detects National Provider Identifiers (ten digits beginning with 1 or 2, validated by the NPI check digit, format 1234567893).

sections.description: Section-based filters. Each entry defines a start/end pattern pair to redact.

state.description: Detects U.S. state names using dictionary matching.

surname.description: Detects surnames/last names using dictionary matching.

trackingNumber.description: Detects shipping tracking numbers (UPS, FedEx, USPS).

zipCode.description: Detects U.S. ZIP codes (5-digit and ZIP+4 formats).

abstractFilterProperties.description: Common properties inherited by all filters.

ignored.description: Specific values to ignore for this filter.

ignoredFiles.description: Paths to files containing values to ignore for this filter.

ignoredPatterns.description: Regex patterns whose matches are ignored by this filter.

windowSize.description: Context window size (number of surrounding tokens to consider).

priority.description: Priority of this filter relative to others. Higher values take precedence.

id.description: Optional identifier for this filter, assigned by the policy author or generated, so the filter can be referenced in logs and diagnostics without printing content that may be PII. Opaque to redaction behavior: it never changes how a document is filtered. Must not itself contain PII.

cueWordFilterProperties.description: Options shared by filters whose values only count next to a cue word, such as a member ID after 'Member ID'. A value matches only when a cue word appears within windowSize tokens before it. Cue words match case-insensitively as whole words, a multi-word cue word as a phrase, and may be followed by punctuation such as ':' or '#'. The cue word itself is not part of the match.

patterns.description: Java-compatible regular expressions for the value. When set, they replace the filter's default pattern instead of adding to it. Each pattern gets the same load-time check and match timeout as the identifier filter's pattern.

cueWords.description: Cue words for this filter. They are added to the filter's default cue words unless defaultCueWords is false.

defaultCueWords.description: Whether the filter's default cue words are used along with cueWords. false is only allowed with at least one entry in cueWords, since otherwise no value could follow a cue word.

baseFilterStrategy.description: Common properties for all filter strategies.

id.description: Optional identifier for this strategy instance, assigned by the policy author or generated, so the strategy and its condition can be referenced in logs and diagnostics without printing content that may be PII. Opaque to redaction behavior: it never changes how a document is filtered. Must not itself contain PII.

redactionFormat.description: Format string for REDACT strategy. Supports placeholders: %t (filter type), %v (original value), %l (label).

replacementScope.description: Scope for consistent replacements. DOCUMENT: same token always gets same replacement within a document. CONTEXT: same token gets same replacement within a context.

maskLength.description: Length of the mask. SAME preserves the original length. Can also be a number for fixed-length masking.

truncateLeaveCharacters.description: Number of characters to leave visible when using TRUNCATE strategy. At most length - 1 characters are kept, so a value no longer than this setting still has at least one character replaced: with the default, ABCD becomes ABC* and AB becomes A*.

truncateCharacter.description: Character used to replace truncated portions.

truncateDirection.description: Which end of the value to truncate.

condition.description: Conditional expression that must be satisfied for this strategy to apply. If every strategy on a filter has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. Supports fields: token, context, confidence, population. Operators: startswith, ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, is, is not. Multiple conditions joined with and. Example: 'confidence > 0.9', 'confidence > 0.5 and confidence < 0.9', 'token startswith "5"', 'population < 4500', 'token is birthdate'.

salt.description: Whether to add a random salt to hashed values (HASH_SHA256_REPLACE).

anonymizationCandidates.description: Custom candidate values for FROM_LIST anonymization method.

mappings.description: MAP_REPLACE lookup table mapping a detected value to its replacement. Inline entries take precedence over any loaded from mappingFiles.

mappingFiles.description: MAP_REPLACE: local file paths (TSV, one tab-delimited key/value pair per row) merged into the lookup table at policy-load time. Inline mappings override entries loaded from files.

caseSensitive.description: MAP_REPLACE: whether lookup-table keys are matched case-sensitively.

generator.description: MAP_REPLACE: name of a generator declared in the top-level generators block, invoked to produce a replacement for a detected value absent from the lookup table.

fallbackStrategy.description: MAP_REPLACE: terminal strategy applied when a detected value is absent from the lookup table and no generator is set, or when the generator fails, times out, or returns invalid output. A detected value is never left in the clear.

color.description: Optional color of the bar drawn over a span redacted by this strategy when rendering a PDF or image. Overrides the policy-wide config.pdf.redactionColor for spans this strategy redacts; when unset, the policy-wide color (default black) applies. Accepts a named color (black, white, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, gray) or a 6-digit hex string matching ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$ (e.g. '#ff8800'); an unrecognized or malformed value renders as black. Has no effect on text redaction.

dateFilterStrategy.description: A filter strategy for date values. Supports all base strategies plus date-specific strategies: TRUNCATE_TO_YEAR, SHIFT, and RELATIVE.

id.description: Optional identifier for this strategy instance, assigned by the policy author or generated, so the strategy and its condition can be referenced in logs and diagnostics without printing content that may be PII. Opaque to redaction behavior: it never changes how a document is filtered. Must not itself contain PII.

strategy.description: The redaction/replacement strategy to apply. Date filters support additional strategies: TRUNCATE_TO_YEAR, SHIFT, and RELATIVE.

redactionFormat.description: Format string for REDACT strategy. Supports placeholders: %t (filter type), %v (original value), %l (label).

maskLength.description: Length of the mask. SAME preserves the original length.

truncateLeaveCharacters.description: Number of characters to leave visible when using TRUNCATE strategy. At most length - 1 characters are kept, so a value no longer than this setting still has at least one character replaced: with the default, ABCD becomes ABC* and AB becomes A*.

truncateCharacter.description: Character used to replace truncated portions.

truncateDirection.description: Which end of the value to truncate.

condition.description: Conditional expression that must be satisfied for this strategy to apply. If every strategy on a filter has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. Date filters support: 'token is birthdate', 'token is deathdate', 'token is birthdate or deathdate'.

salt.description: Whether to add a random salt to hashed values.

anonymizationCandidates.description: Custom candidate values for FROM_LIST anonymization method.

shiftRandom.description: Whether to shift dates by a random amount (SHIFT strategy).

shiftDays.description: Number of days to shift dates (SHIFT strategy).

shiftMonths.description: Number of months to shift dates (SHIFT strategy).

shiftYears.description: Number of years to shift dates (SHIFT strategy).

futureDates.description: Whether shifted dates may land in the future (SHIFT strategy).

color.description: Optional color of the bar drawn over a span redacted by this strategy when rendering a PDF or image. Overrides the policy-wide config.pdf.redactionColor for spans this strategy redacts; when unset, the policy-wide color (default black) applies. Accepts a named color (black, white, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, gray) or a 6-digit hex string matching ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$ (e.g. '#ff8800'); an unrecognized or malformed value renders as black. Has no effect on text redaction.

generators.description: Map of generator name to its definition. A MAP_REPLACE strategy references a generator by name to produce a replacement for a detected value absent from its lookup table.

generator.description: A named replacement generator. Targets a local model endpoint inside the deployment boundary so detected values are not sent to a third party.

type.description: Generator backend. 'ollama' calls a local Ollama-compatible generate endpoint.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the local generator endpoint (e.g. 'http://localhost:11434'). Must resolve inside the deployment boundary.

model.description: Model name the endpoint should use (e.g. 'llama3.1').

prompt.description: Prompt template. The placeholder {{token}} is replaced with the detected value and {{label}} with its entity label. The model must return only the replacement value.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the generator before falling back to the strategy's fallbackStrategy. Required so a generator can never block the pipeline indefinitely.

ageFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected age values. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

bankRoutingNumberFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected bank routing numbers. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

bitcoinFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected Bitcoin addresses. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

filterCanadaSin.description: Detects Canadian Social Insurance Numbers (nine digits, Luhn-validated, format NNN-NNN-NNN).

canadaSinFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected SINs. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

onlyValidPrefixes.description: Do not detect SINs beginning with 0 or 8, which are not issued to individuals (8 is used for business numbers, which also pass the Luhn check). Default false (match any Luhn-valid nine-digit value).

filterCity.description: Detects city names using dictionary matching.

cityFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected city names. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

fuzzy.description: Enable fuzzy matching for approximate matches.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity level controlling match strictness when fuzzy matching is enabled.

capitalized.description: Only match capitalized variants of city names.

filterCounty.description: Detects county names using dictionary matching.

countyFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected county names. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

fuzzy.description: Enable fuzzy matching for approximate matches.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity level controlling match strictness when fuzzy matching is enabled.

capitalized.description: Only match capitalized variants of county names.

creditCardFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected credit card numbers. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format. To transform every detected value, end with a strategy that has no condition.

onlyValidCreditCardNumbers.description: Only detect numbers that pass Luhn checksum validation.

ignoreWhenInUnixTimestamp.description: Ignore sequences that appear to be Unix timestamps.

onlyWordBoundaries.description: Only detect numbers at word boundaries.

currencyFilterStrategies.description: Strategies for handling detected currency values. Strategies are evaluated in order, and the first one with no condition or a satisfied condition is applied. If every strategy has a condition and none is satisfied, the value is left unchanged. If no strategies are given, the value is redacted with the default format.
